Orinti Explains Web Site Updates

 

SAN DIEGO (May 2)—Orinti, Inc., one of North America's largest purveyors of tea, recently added a page to its Web site, listing the sources of all the tea leaves that end up in its final products. The page was created in response to recent public scrutiny over whether the company is justified in claiming that its tea is pesticide-free.

 

    “The rumors being circulated do not reflect reality,” Orinti CEO Giovanni Shaw said in a public statement issued on Tuesday. “We procure tea leaves only from producers who meet our strict quality standards. We never settle for anything less.”

 

     According to Mr. Shaw, the company also utilizes software that tracks the producer, the processing date, and other pertinent data for each batch of tea leaves.

 

     “This level of detail is not displayed on our packaging for the simple reason that we do not have the space for it,” said Mr. Shaw. “As we are committed to transparency, this information can be viewed on our Web site.”

 

     The popular blog foodnews.org was the first to call into question Orinti's assertion that its tea leaves are grown without the use of pesticides. The issue has since attracted national attention.

In the Kitchen

Reviewed by Peter Gottlieb

 

Qi Chien understands how restaurants work. Her new book, In the Kitchen: How to Thrive in the Restaurant Business, expertly advises restaurant managers on handling challenges in the industry, from creating reasonable schedules for chefs to appeasing picky diners. Throughout the book, Chien offers concise, practical suggestions with easy-to-understand concepts. Overall, the book offers a colorful snapshot of the various tasks involved in the day-to-day operations of a restaurant.

 

Chien's book is unique among other industry guides in that she interviewed restaurant owners, managers, and customers as part of her research. She even spoke to journalists who write restaurant reviews to get a good sense of what they most prize in a dining experience. My only criticism is that the book should have also included the perspective of chefs, especially since their role is crucial to a restaurant's success. This caveat aside, In the Kitchen is an insightful and instructive read.

From: qichien@rapidonline.com

Subject: In the Kitchen

 

To the Editor:

 

I was delighted to read Peter Gottlieb's review of my latest book, In the Kitchen, in your newspaper. I have appreciated his thoughtful comments about my works over the years, even if they are sometimes negative. In this case, I was especially glad that he liked the chapter about restaurant reviewers, since initially I had been reluctant to interview journalists for the book. It is true that I could have included a greater variety of insights, but unfortunately the people whose views he most wanted to hear were just too busy to speak with me before the publishing deadline. Perhaps this is something I can address in an updated edition of the book.

 

Qi Chien

Thank you for agreeing to work with the team at Cybernetic Robotics as they tested their new robot, Deonardo, in our hospital. As you know, Deonardo was developed to allow you, our nursing staff, more time to focus on patients. This is exciting work.

It has been a month, and Cybernetic Robotics would like to hear about your experiences with Deonardo. Please use the following link to complete an online survey. www.cyberneticrobotics.com/survey/everlast/

Gretchen Robertson

Director, Everlast Hospital

https://www.cyberneticrobotics.com/survey/everlast/01282

Deonardo is easy to work with. I like that I don't have to tell Deonardo directly what to do. When I update patient information in our system, Deonardo's tasks are updated as well. I have been better able to concentrate on my patients because I know Deonardo takes care of little things that used to take up so much of my time. Deonardo was particularly helpful during a recent state review because it delivered patients' medications for all the nurses so that we didn't have to, and we were able to focus on patient care. questions.stem: What does the speaker expect one of the listeners to do?

questions.stem: Who most likely is the speaker?

questions.stem: What does the speaker say she needs the listener to do?

questions.stem: Why does the speaker say, “we're offering a workshop on that topic next month''?

questions.stem: Please arrive ten minutes before your appointment to allow enough ------ to fill out some paperwork.

questions.stem: The printed ------ for the upcoming musical are kept in the theater director’s office.

questions.stem: Laboratory chemicals should be stored no ------ than eye level and never on top of a tall cabinet.

questions.stem: Because airlines ------ revise baggage-check policies, passengers should check for updates before a flight.

questions.stem: Contracts for the Queen’s Landing project should be placed in an ------ stack on the supervisor’s desk.

questions.stem: Some board members ------ that Mr. Saito’s sales forecasts are too optimistic.

questions.stem: Ms. Koffler is confident ------ the new manager will improve the department’s productivity.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc "confident that + clause" dùng để thể hiện sự tin tưởng vào một sự việc nào đó sẽ xảy ra.

questions.stem: The wooden barn on the Eastwood property is so ------ deteriorated that it is unlikely to be salvaged.
questions.explanation: Trạng từ "badly" thường đi kèm với các động từ chỉ sự hư hỏng để nhấn mạnh mức độ trầm trọng (badly deteriorated - hư hỏng nặng).

questions.stem: Roseville Resort is offering discounted accommodations ------ its first month of operation.
questions.explanation: Giới từ "during" (trong suốt) dùng để chỉ khoảng thời gian (tháng hoạt động đầu tiên) mà chương trình giảm giá diễn ra.

questions.stem: Although the look of the new mobile phone model is ------ the previous one, the call quality is much improved.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc "similar to" (tương tự với) dùng để so sánh vẻ ngoài của mẫu điện thoại mới với mẫu trước đó.

questions.stem: Dr. Simone Beaumont ------ to head of Research and Development at Brodeur Technology last week.

questions.stem: Enertek Industries is developing an ------ safe method for refining lithium.

questions.stem: Before starting the motor, make sure the brake is ------.
questions.explanation: Chỗ trống đứng sau động từ "is", cần một tính từ hoặc phân từ đóng vai trò tính từ. "Engaged" (đã được khớp/vào nấc) là trạng thái của phanh.

questions.stem: Henderson Technical College offers introductory computer ------ for free to community members.
questions.explanation: "Computer lessons" (các bài học máy tính) là cụm từ phù hợp nhất trong bối cảnh trường cao đẳng kỹ thuật cung cấp cho cộng đồng.

questions.stem: No fees will be charged for the time the agency ------ to search for records.
questions.explanation: Cấu trúc "takes time to do something" (tốn thời gian để làm gì). "Takes" là động từ phù hợp nhất khi nói về thời gian cần thiết.

questions.stem: The Durand Concert Hall, ------ was built 80 years ago, has undergone a complete renovation.
questions.explanation: "Which" là đại từ quan hệ dùng để thay thế cho danh từ chỉ vật "The Durand Concert Hall" và làm chủ ngữ cho mệnh đề quan hệ.

questions.stem: There may be flaws in the computer code that we are not------aware of.
questions.explanation: "Not yet aware of" (vẫn chưa nhận thức được) là cấu trúc phổ biến. "Yet" thường dùng trong câu phủ định để chỉ một sự việc chưa xảy ra.

questions.stem: ------ who wishes to make a monetary gift to the Voltra Museum should fill out the form at the back of the brochure.
questions.explanation: "Anyone" (bất kỳ ai) là đại từ bất định làm chủ ngữ phù hợp nhất đứng trước mệnh đề quan hệ "who wishes...".
